'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray War]], [[Sexual violence in the Tigray War]]
**The [[United Nations Security Council]] declares its concern about the war in [[Ethiopia]]'s [[Tigray Region]] for the first time since the conflict began, particularly because of the use of sexual violence by security forces against civilian women and girls. The statement drafted by [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] has been approved unanimously by the council. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/un-security-council-notes-concern-over-humanitarian-situation-tigray-2021-04-22/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
**[[Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association]] Chairman [[Akio Toyoda]] announces that the 2021 [[Tokyo Motor Show]] will be cancelled due to [[COVID-19]]. It is the first cancellation in the event's history. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/04/22/business/corporate-business/tokyo-motor-show-cancel/ (''The Japan Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports 314,835 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, which is a world record for daily cases, thereby bringing the total of confirmed cases to 15.9 million. The country also reports a record 2,104 deaths, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 184,657. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/india-covid-global-record-one-day-rise-cases-314000/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****[[Japan]] reports its first five cases of the "double mutant" Lineage B.1.617 variant first detected in [[India]]. [https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2021042201037/ (Nippon.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record seven deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 117. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-thailand/thailand-reports-1470-coronavirus-cases-daily-record-7-deaths-idUSL4N2MF12T?fbclid=IwAR0ds-8Bxeay_SkBkPjdCLLABDHbHADMdzANu9K3AjsfuAVAgqpdslSRYGo (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
****The number of [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccines]] administered in the [[United Arab Emirates]] surpasses 10 million doses. [https://amp.khaleejtimes.com/coronavirus-pandemic/covid-19-uaes-vaccination-crosses-10-million-mark (Khaleej Times)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****[[Belgium]] reports its first cases of the Lineage B.1.617 variant in a group of [[India]]n [[nursing student]]s who travelled from [[Paris]]. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/indian-covid-variant-detected-in-belgium-health-official-01619120714 (''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] surpasses 10 million people who have received at least one dose of the COVID-19 vaccine. [https://cadenaser.com/ser/2021/04/22/sociedad/1619103550_972863.html (Cadena Ser)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
*****[[Alberta]] reports its first case of the Lineage B.1.617 variant that fuelled surge in [[India]] in a returning inter-provincial traveler. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/deena-hinshaw-covid-alberta-1.5997777 (CBC)]
****[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****The [[Government of Canada|Canadian government]] announces that [[Canada|the country]] will ban all travel from [[India]] and [[Pakistan]] due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases in those countries. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/flight-ban-india-1.5997880 (CBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****The U.S. surpasses 32 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.nbcsandiego.com/news/national-international/32-million-covid-19-cases-in-us-since-start-of-pandemic/2584718/ (KNSD)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Western Sahara]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic]], [[Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic–Spain relations]]
*****The [[Polisario Front]] reports that [[Brahim Ghali]], the [[President of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic|president]] of the [[Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic]], has been hospitalized in Spain for COVID-19 treatment. The [[Government of Spain|Spanish government]] states his entry was permitted strictly on humanitarian grounds. [https://apnews.com/article/spain-government-and-politics-africa-europe-7b6b5ebdfecd96ccc7754b4ba6dcc321 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo]]
****The [[North Kivu]] province in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] will begin its [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccination]] campaign, with around 60,000 doses arriving in [[Goma]]. This comes after the country's announcement that it will kick off uts own vaccination campaign by using [[AstraZeneca]]'s [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2021/04/23/drc-s-north-kivu-to-start-covid-vaccinations/ (Africanews)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] reports a record 537 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 60,620. [https://www.clarin.com/sociedad/coronavirus-argentina-confirman-27-216-nuevos-casos-ultimas-24-horas_0_TX05XlLhk.html (''Clarín'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–United Kingdom relations]], [[Uyghur genocide]]
**The [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|UK House of Commons]] unanimously passes a non-binding resolution condemning the [[Xinjiang internment camps|internment]] of [[Uyghurs]] as genocide. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/22/world/uk-china-uyghur-genocide-motion-gbr-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
**The [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Russian Defense Ministry]] announces that it will move [[Russian Ground Forces|its forces]] away from the [[Russia–Ukraine border|Ukrainian border]] beginning tomorrow. [[Ukraine]] and its western allies accused [[Russia]] of trying to provoke conflict by moving troops to the border, while Defense Minister [[Sergey Shoygu]] claimed that it was only to conduct drills. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/22/russia-orders-pullback-of-troops-after-military-drills (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[United States]] hosts a two-day Leaders Summit on Climate and invites 40 world leaders to discuss the necessity of combating climate change and committing to reduce their nations' emissions. Due to quarantine protocols, the conference is virtual. [https://www.cnn.com/politics/live-news/biden-climate-change-summit-04-22-22/h_04010e2eb0fad09a7680694a83353c22 (CNN)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]], [[Killing of Ma'Khia Bryant]]
**Demonstrations spread throughout [[Columbus (Ohio)|Columbus]] the day after 16-year-old Ma'Khia Bryant was shot and killed by a [[Columbus Division of Police|Columbus police officer]], demanding police accountability. During a vigil for Ma'Khia, local activist Hana Abdur Rahim called for the [[Police abolition movement|abolition of the police system]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2021/04/22/columbus-police-shot-killed-makhia-bryant-what-we-know/7331811002/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
**[[President of Germany|President]] [[Frank-Walter Steinmeier]] signs into law changes to the Infectious Diseases Protection Act that will give the [[Government of Germany|federal government]] the power to impose "emergency brake" measures in areas where the infection rate exceeds certain levels. The signing comes after the [[Bundesrat of Germany|Bundesrat]] gave its final approval for the controversial law. [https://www.dw.com/en/german-president-signs-national-coronavirus-rules-into-law/a-57272234 (DW)]
*[[2021 Boulder shooting]]
**Ahmad Al Aliwi Al-Issa, the suspect in last month's [[mass shooting]] in [[Boulder, Colorado]], faces more than 40 additional charges in relation to the incident. The new charges include attempted first-degree murder, first-degree assault, and using a [[high-capacity magazine]], which is illegal in [[Colorado]]. [https://www.npr.org/2021/04/22/989715457/boulder-supermarket-shooting-suspect-faces-dozens-of-new-charges (NPR)] [https://apnews.com/article/boulder-shootings-colorado-ahmad-al-aliwi-alissa-denver-af173b8bcca7ff1b8615f379dd879229 (AP)]
*Letters with [[CETME rifle]] bullets are received by the [[Ministry of the Interior (Spain)|Spanish Minister of the Interior]] [[Fernando Grande-Marlaska]], the leader of [[Podemos (Spanish political party)|Podemos]] [[Pablo Iglesias Turrión|Pablo Iglesias]] and the general director of the [[Civil Guard (Spain)|Civil Guard]] María Gámez. The death threats are condemned by [[Prime Minister of Spain|Spanish Prime Minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/spanish-pm-condemns-death-threat-against-minister-01619123725?tesla=y (''Barron's'')]
*Three of the seven [[Catholic Church in Haiti|Catholic]] [[Clergy#Catholicism|clergy]] who were kidnapped in [[Croix-des-Bouquets]], [[Ouest (department)|Ouest]], [[Haiti]], on April 11 are released. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1422836/three-of-seven-catholic-clergy-kidnapped-in-haiti-are-released (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Xenophobia and racism related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The [[United States Senate]] votes 94–1 to pass the COVID-19 Hate Crimes Act with bipartisan changes. The bill, which would expedite anti-Asian hate crime reviews to the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]], will next head to the [[United States House of Representatives]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2021/04/22/covid-19-hate-crime-bill-protect-asian-americans-passes-senate/7290109002/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[Statehood movement in the District of Columbia]], [[DC Admission Act]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives]] votes 216–208 to pass a bill that would make [[Washington, D.C.]] the [[51st state]], with general support from Democrats and opposition from Republicans. [https://apnews.com/article/district-of-columbia-race-and-ethnicity-government-and-politics-legislation-frederick-douglass-9edf21fe93e813808f1488ceb0b7900b (AP)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[NASA]]'s [[Perseverance (rover)|''Perseverance'' rover]] successfully synthesizes breathable [[oxygen]] while on the surface of [[Mars]]. This demonstrates the feasibility of [[In-situ resource utilization|locally producing oxygen]] for human [[life support system|life support]] and [[liquid oxygen#In rocket propellant|propellant production]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mars-perseverance-rover-oxygen-nasa/ (CBS News)]
